item.name: CI Smoke
item.description: Deterministic, non-destructive requests safe to run unattended against DEV/TEST/STG. /health touches nothing (see services/api/koras_api/routers/health.py); /platform-health reads only.

request.description: No auth required. Source: services/api/koras_api/routers/health.py health().
Read-only. Requires PlatformReadDep -- a platform staff token. Source: routers/health.py platform_health().

exec: pm.test('status field is ok or degraded', () => pm.expect(['ok','degraded']).to.include(pm.response.json().status));
pm.test.skip('no access_token set in the environment');

item.name: Security & Negative Tests
item.description: Grounded in services/api/koras_api/core/auth.py and organization_auth.py. Verification and authorisation are kept apart there on purpose: an unverifiable token is 401, a verified caller lacking authority is 403 -- these requests assert that split rather than guessing at it.

item.name: Missing Authorization header is refused (403, FastAPI HTTPBearer default)

request.description: HTTPBearer(auto_error=True) raises 403 'Not authenticated' when no Authorization header is present -- FastAPI's own default (fastapi/security/http.py), not a KORAS-specific code. Deliberately different from an invalid token (401, below): a request that never tried to authenticate is not the same failure as one that tried and failed.

exec: pm.test('missing auth is refused with 403', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

request.description: Source: core/auth.py _verified() -- a TokenVerificationError is answered as 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, logged (not returned) so a forged token and an expired one look identical to the caller.

exec: pm.test('invalid token is refused with 401', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: Unknown organization id is never answered with 200

request.description: A syntactically valid but non-existent id. Requires a platform token. Asserts the API does not answer 200 with someone else's data for a guessed id -- it does not assert one specific refusal code, because that is the router's to define and this test must not invent one.

exec: pm.test('unknown organization id is never answered with 200', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.not.equal(200));
} else { pm.test.skip('no access_token set in the environment'); }

item.name: Malformed payload on create is refused with 422

request.description: name must be a string and slug is required (see routers/organizations.py request schema). FastAPI's Pydantic validation refuses a wrong-typed/missing field before the route body ever runs -- a framework guarantee, not app logic.

exec: pm.test('malformed payload is refused with 422', () => pm.response.to.have.status(422));
} else { pm.test.skip('no access_token set in the environment'); }
